forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: South Holland's auditor KPMG expects to issue a qualified opinion on the council's 2025/26 accounts
news_drafts.lead:
South Holland District Council's external auditor, the accountancy firm KPMG, expects to issue a qualified opinion on the council's 2025/26 accounts. A qualified audit opinion means the auditor could not fully sign off the accounts. The auditor expects the report to be modified.

The statement is in KPMG's draft report to the council's Governance and Audit Committee, which meets on 12 November 2026. The auditor writes: "due to the statutory backstop date of 31 January 2027, we will be issuing a qualified opinion." The paper gives the reason as the progress of the current-year audit together with that date.

The draft report says the basis for the qualified opinion will be set out in KPMG's final report. The papers give no figures on the accounts themselves.

news_drafts.headline: South Holland removes waste scheme funding risk with £1.2m allocation confirmed for 2025-26
news_drafts.lead: South Holland has secured confirmation of its government funding allocation for waste collection under the Extended Producer Responsibility scheme, removing a source of budget uncertainty. The council has received formal notification of £1,231,000 for 2025-26, drawn from a government guarantee of £1.1 billion to local authorities for packaging waste collection. This resolves a previously unquantified budget pressure. The council nonetheless maintains its budget risk at High overall, citing continuing pressures from government funding reduction, income loss, capital spending demands, and the Internal Drainage Board levy, alongside inflation and fuel costs. The council's mitigation relies on its medium-term financial strategy and a sound level of reserves.

findings.headline: The government's September 2026 decision reviews Lincolnshire's reorganisation, and bodies have been asked to cease LGR implementation work until the review is complete.
findings.detail: The paper records a July 2026 decision to create two new unitary authorities in Lincolnshire, expected to go live in April 2028. It reports that in September 2026 the government decided to review this and asked all bodies to stop implementation work.
findings.matters: A finance director at any council in a reorganisation area needs to know that the timetable and the structure of the authority are now in review, which affects planning for reserves, debt and transition costs.
findings.figures: Shadow authority elections expected in 2027; new authorities expected April 2028; decision dates July 2026 and September 2026
findings.quote: In September 2026 a decision was taken by government to review their decision in Lincolnshire and other regions, and all bodies have been asked to cease work on LGR implementation until that review is complete.

findings.headline: The Council describes reliance on reserves as "unsustainable over the long term" and says reserves currently provide a sufficient buffer while it diversifies its income
findings.detail: The Narrative Report says the reserves currently provide a sufficient buffer to meet ongoing pressures and finance transformation projects. It states the Council is therefore diversifying its income and exploring additional financial strategies.
findings.matters: A council stating in its audited accounts that its reserves cannot carry it indefinitely, and setting out a diversification response, is a position a lender or peer finance director will want to track.
findings.figures: No specific figures are given in this statement
findings.quote: While our reserves currently provide a sufficient buffer to meet ongoing pressures and finance transformation projects, relying solely on these reserves is unsustainable over the long term.

findings.headline: The General Fund reserve balance is £11.599m, after a net transfer to reserves of £0.846m.
findings.detail: The Narrative Report states that the transfer covers revenue and capital expenditure. The Movement in Reserves Statement shows General Fund balance held at £2,078k and General Fund earmarked reserves rising from £8,675k to £9,521k.
findings.matters: The General Fund reserve rising at the same time as the outturn underspend is a position a finance director can compare with their own reserve strategy.
findings.figures: General Fund reserve balance £11.599m; net transfer to reserves £0.846m; General Fund earmarked reserves £8,675k rising to £9,521k
findings.quote: The General Fund reserve balance is £11.599m, after a net transfer to reserves of £0.846m to cover revenue and capital expenditure.

findings.headline: The HRA capital programme outturn is £11.976m against a revised budget of £20.356m.
findings.detail: The largest underspend is Renewable Energy, with £2.950m spent against £8.309m budgeted. The Decent Homes subtotal is £4.437m against a £6.153m budget, and the funding table shows External Borrowing of £nil against £6.602m budgeted.
findings.matters: A housing capital programme funded to a planned £6.602m of external borrowing that drew none, while renewable energy works ran well below budget, is a position lenders to HRA-holding councils look at closely.
findings.figures: Revised budget £20,356k; draft outturn £11,976k; variance £(8,380)k; Renewable Energy £8,309k budget against £2,950k outturn; External Borrowing £6,602k budgeted, £nil outturn

findings.headline: The 2025/26 capital programme outturn is £11.598m against a revised budget of £14.903m.
findings.detail: The Health and Wellbeing Hub recorded £8.966m against a £10.163m budget. Grants fund £10.544m of the outturn and internal borrowing £0.800m against a revised £2.708m.
findings.matters: Capital spending £3.305m below revised budget, with internal borrowing well below the planned amount, is a position finance directors and lenders watch when judging a council's borrowing need.
findings.figures: Revised budget £14,903k; outturn £11,598k; variance £(3,305)k; Health and Wellbeing Hub outturn £8,966k against £10,163k; internal borrowing £800k against revised £2,708k
